intro: Safeguarding children is everyone's responsibility, and even supporting adults you may be one of the few outsiders who sees a child at risk.
points: Your job is to notice, be curious, record factually and report promptly — never to investigate or confront a parent.
If a child is in immediate danger, call 999; otherwise tell your Designated Safeguarding Lead without delay.
Never promise a child secrecy; listen calmly, use their own words, and reassure them it is not their fault.
Know the four abuse categories — physical, emotional, sexual and neglect — and that a child may face several at once.
Stay alert to harm beyond the home, including child exploitation, county lines, online abuse, FGM and radicalisation.
Fear of breaching data protection is never a reason to leave a child at risk — share what is necessary and proportionate.
